title: Traffic orchestration fallbacks and runbook notes
content:
Purpose and scope:

This working note documents pragmatic fallback patterns and embedded operational runbooks for the control plane and routing layer in multi-region deployments. It’s intended for platform engineers, on-call SREs, and anyone troubleshooting routing/control-plane incidents. The focus is on actionable steps (detect, mitigate, verify, escalate) and safe defaults for cross-region traffic orchestration.

Context and goals:
- Problem space: partial region outages, control-plane API instability, traffic routing loops, model-variant regressions, and noisy-neighbor saturation that impact inference availability or latency.
- Goal: Provide low-friction, repeatable mitigation steps that minimize blast radius and provide clear verification criteria.
- Non-goal: This is not a full postmortem or root-cause analysis; those live in Confluence and Jira (linked artifacts).

Quick architecture recap (operational lens):
- Control plane: central API for route rules, traffic weights, rollout orchestration, and policy evaluation. It writes desired state to per-region agents and metrics collectors.
- Data plane (regional): inference pods, autoscaling groups, local cache (KV/prefix), and request proxies.
- Routing policies: latency-priority, cost-priority, affinity-by-customer, capacity-tiered (Dedicated vs Hosted fallback), and canary/gradual rollouts.
- Safeguards: circuit-breakers, per-route rate limits, automatic fallback to compatible model variants, and region-fallback (policy precedence).

Key operational primitives we rely on:
- Traffic weights: distribution percentages per route variant/region.
- Fallback rules: ordered list where the control plane will try next compatible variant/region on failure.
- Circuit breaker thresholds: consecutive errors, p95 latency, and token loss rate.
- Health probes: control-plane agent health, model-liveness, and KV cache readiness.

Observability checklist (dashboards & metrics to inspect first):
- Per-route: request_rate, error_rate (5xx, model-validation-failures), p50/p95/p99 latency, token_rate.
- Control plane: api_latency_ms, reconciliation_lag_seconds, config_errors, last_successful_sync.
- Region health: region_cpu_utilization, gpu_utilization, queue_backlog, cache_hit_ratio.
- Autoscaling: active_replicas, scaling_events, pod_restart_count.
- Traces: recent traces for failed requests (look for long retries, timeout cascades).

Runbook pattern: severity, trigger, immediate mitigation, durable mitigation, verify, post-incident notes.

Runbook A: Control-plane API degraded / write failures
- Typical triggers:
  - alert: control_plane_api_error_rate > 1% for 2m OR reconciliation_lag_seconds > 45s
  - users report inability to roll out canaries or changes not propagating to regions
- Severity: P1 if reconciliation_lag > 5m and traffic policies are changing frequently; else P2.
- Immediate mitigation (first 5 minutes):
  1) Announce incident in #platform-oncall and tag on-call.
  2) Switch to read-only mode for non-essential control-plane writes (disable automated CI/PR-driven updates).
  3) If the API frontend is overloaded, scale API frontend pods (k8s autoscale override) or enable an emergency replica pool behind the load balancer. Command examples: kubectl scale deployment controlplane-api --replicas=6 -n platform || trigger autoscaler override.
  4) Check persistent store (etcd/postgres) health: pg_isready / etcdctl endpoint health. If datastore is the issue, fail open to cached desired state (agents keep last good config).
- Durable mitigation (10–60 minutes):
  1) Roll back the last control-plane release if the problem started after a deploy: github PR check and revert.
  2) If queues back up, temporarily increase reconciliation interval on agents to reduce write pressure. Example: set agent.reconcile_interval=30s -> 120s via emergency flag.
  3) Throttle non-critical automated flows (CI/CD, infra jobs) by applying a feature-flag to pause them.
- Verification:
  - reconciliation_lag_seconds returns to baseline; last_successful_sync updated for all regions.
  - manual config change applied and observed in target region within expected propagation window.
- Post-incident:
  - Run retrospective to determine whether circuit breaker thresholds need tuning and whether read-only mode should be automated earlier.

Runbook B: Regional GPU saturation / noisy neighbor causing high latencies
- Typical triggers:
  - High gpu_utilization > 90% + p95 latency spike for region X
  - Autoscaler failing to add capacity or pods stuck pending for > 2m
- Severity: P1 for customer-impacting sustained errors; P2 if transient.
- Immediate mitigation:
  1) Shift non-affinity traffic off the impacted region by adjusting traffic weights on the route to 0% for region X and add capacity in another region. Quick control-plane API call example: PATCH /routes/{route_id}/weights {"region_x":0,"region_y":100}.
  2) If weight changes are blocked by control-plane issues, apply local proxy-level traffic deny or return 503 to force clients to retry elsewhere.
  3) If a single tenant is responsible (identified by high token-rate on tenant_id), apply per-tenant rate limit to throttle.
- Durable mitigation:
  1) Spin up dedicated reserved capacity if noisy-neighbor is recurring (escalate to sales for Dedicated offering).
  2) Investigate autoscaler logs and pod events; fix scheduling constraints (taints/tolerations) or increase GPU quota in cloud account.
- Verification:
  - p95 latency in region X drops to baseline and queue_backlog reduces.
  - No increase in error_rate after reroute.

Runbook C: Model variant regression (new model variant returns higher error or hallucination rate)
- Typical triggers:
  - Regression alert from quality monitor or customer-reported regressions; sudden spike in model-validation-failures metric.
- Severity: P1 if production traffic is impacted or quality SLAs violated.
- Immediate mitigation:
  1) Stop the rollout: set variant weight -> 0% (control-plane traffic-weight update).
  2) Automatically fail back to previously known-good variant (we keep the last stable pinned).
  3) Pin inference calls for affected tenant(s) to hosted stable variant via per-tenant override.
- Durable mitigation:
  1) Run targeted evals and compare prompts that triggered regressions. Add failing prompt set to regression suite.
  2) Restrict future rollouts by increasing canary duration and reducing initial weight.
- Verification:
  - quality_monitoring.alerts clear, customer-reports stop, compare score delta to acceptance threshold.

Runbook D: Routing policy misconfiguration (rules cause unintended amplification or loops)
- Typical triggers:
  - sudden increase in internal retries, duplicated requests, or unexpected traffic spikes between regions
  - config linter produced warnings, or config change recently merged
- Severity: P1 if causes broader outage or cost surge.
- Immediate mitigation:
  1) Revert offending control-plane config change. Use: controlplane rollback-config --to=commit_id.
  2) If rollback is not possible, apply emergency guard rule at ingress proxies: drop requests matching offending headers or route-patterns.
  3) Reduce retry counts and increase retry jitter globally until stable.
- Durable mitigation:
  1) Add stronger schema validation to control-plane API and a pre-deploy simulator that checks for loops and amplification patterns.
  2) Establish automated cost-guard alerting (budget burn %).
- Verification:
  - duplication/loop metrics return to baseline; cost-rate normalizes.

Runbook E: Multi-region failover test gone wrong (canary rollout created cross-region chase)
- Scenario: a gradual canary unintentionally routes small percentage to region with cold caches causing high tail latency and then control-plane retries chase that region.
- Immediate mitigation:
  1) Pause or pause-and-rewind the rollout: set canary weight -> 0%.
  2) Warm caches in target region via synthetic traffic at low priority (cache-warm job) before resuming.
  3) If synthetic warmup is not possible, redirect traffic to warm region until cache hit ratio > threshold.
- Verification:
  - cache_hit_ratio increases; p99 latency decreases.

Operational knobs and safe values (starting defaults that should be tuned per workload):
- circuit_breaker: consecutive_errors=5, reset_interval=30s, half_open_attempts=3.
- default_retry: 1 retry with exponential backoff starting 100ms up to 1s.
- canary_policy: initial_weight=2%, step_size=5% every 10m, abort_on_error_threshold=1% error_rate above baseline.
- region_failover_delay: 30s (short to avoid user-visible errors but long enough to avoid flapping).

Automation helpers (cheat-sheet commands and API examples):
- Query reconciliation lag: curl -sS https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/health | jq .reconciliation_lag_seconds
- Set route weights (example): curl -X PATCH https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/routes/route-abc/weights -d '{"weights":{"us-east-1":0,"us-west-2":100}}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN'
- Pause rollout: curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/rollouts/rollout-123/pause
- Force agent to re-sync (per-region): ssh agent-host && sudo systemctl restart controlplane-agent

Escalation contacts (on-call primary then platform leads):
- On-call: #platform-oncall (rotation info in PagerDuty)
- Platform lead: Daniel Park (pager)
- Serving runtime: Priya Nair
- Applied ML: Miguel Santos

Post-incident checklist (to attach to Jira postmortem):
1) Timeline of events with exact control-plane commands and who executed them.
2) Metric dump for before/during/after windows (store as CSV).
3) Root cause hypothesis and supporting evidence.
4) Action items: config changes, automation, tests, alerts tuning.
5) Owner and target date for each action.

Small experiments and TODOs (open items for platform team):
- TODO: Implement a "safe-mode" that automatically lowers non-critical traffic weights when reconciliation_lag > threshold. (Jira PLAT-4321)
- TODO: Add a simulation harness that replays production RPS against new routing rules in a sandbox to detect loops.
- Experiment: Evaluate using quantified request scoring to route by expected token cost rather than pure latency for cost-sensitive customers.

Notes and open questions:
- How often should read-only mode be auto-triggered? Tradeoff: false positives block legitimate config changes. Need threshold tuning.
- Can we provide tenants an API to opt out of cross-region failover for latency-sensitive applications? (privacy/data residency concerns)

Appendix: quick reference
- emergency steps (1-line): announce -> pause rollouts -> reduce weights on impacted region -> verify metrics -> execute durable mitigation -> open postmortem.
- critical dashboards: Console > Observability > Per-route | Console > Platform > Control Plane Health | Console > Regions > GPU Utilization
- important metrics: reconciliation_lag_seconds, control_plane_api_error_rate, per_route_error_rate, region_gpu_utilization, cache_hit_ratio

This is a working document. If you update any operational steps here, please add a changelog entry at the top and ping #platform-oncall.

End of doc.
